title: Lesson 4: Divide by 9 — The Running Remainder Trick
learningGoals: Understand why 9 has a special pattern in division.
Apply the running-remainder trick to divide any number by 9 mentally.
Handle cases where the running remainder exceeds 9.
coreIdeas: To divide by 9: bring down the first digit as the first quotient digit.
Each subsequent quotient digit = previous quotient digit + next dividend digit.
The final remainder = sum of all quotient digits subtracted if it exceeds 9.
The remainder is the last running sum (reduced if ≥ 9).

workedExamples.method: First digit=1 (quotient). Remainder: 1+2=3. Quotient=1, Remainder=3. Check: 9×1+3=12. Correct.
Q1=1. Running: 1+3=4. Running: 4+2=6. Quotient=14, Remainder=6. Check: 9×14+6=126+6=132.
Q1=1. 1+2=3. 3+3=6. 6+4=10 → remainder=10≥9, adjust: quotient becomes 137, remainder=10−9=1. Answer: 137 r 1.
Q1=2. 2+3=5. 5+4=9 → remainder=9, adjust: quotient 26, remainder=0. Answer: 26 r 0.

starterPractice: Guided: Divide 23 by 9 using the running sum trick.
Independent: Divide 132 by 9 using three steps.

exercises.questionText: If 1338 ÷ 9 = Q R 6, what is Q?
exercises.hint: Use the check: dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder. So 1338 = 9 × Q + 6.
exercises.solution: Subtract the remainder first: 1338 − 6 = 1332. Then divide by 9: 1332 ÷ 9 = 148. Check: 9 × 148 + 6 = 1332 + 6 = 1338.
